aspects.says: An exception in a response or request listener ends in the adaptor's receiver thread and drops the link; a callback catches its own failures and hands them on.
basis: section:9.4 An Exception in a jPOS Callback Drops the Link and Reaches No Caller

aspects.says: Field 39 is read from the network's list: approvals other than 00, try later as a new transaction, format errors as the developers' problem.
basis: section:9.3 Field 39 Says Who Acts Next

aspects.says: A calling thread sees four endings: an ISOException and isConnected() false mean the host saw nothing, a response means it decided, and null means nobody knows.
basis: section:9.1 Your Thread Sees Four Endings, and Each Says What the Host Knows

aspects.says: With ignore-iso-exceptions the link survives a packing error, but the bad message still ends as null after the full timeout.
basis: section:9.2 A Field the Packager Refuses Fails on the Adaptor's Thread, and Takes the Link With It

aspects.says: A field the packager refuses fails on the adaptor's sender thread, drops the link by default and reaches the caller only as null; packing a copy first turns it into a refusal before sending.
basis: section:9.2 A Field the Packager Refuses Fails on the Adaptor's Thread, and Takes the Link With It

aspects.says: A packager checks lengths, not content, so a value of the right length can still be wrong.
basis: section:9.2 A Field the Packager Refuses Fails on the Adaptor's Thread, and Takes the Link With It

aspects.says: A Spring @ControllerAdvice never sees an exception on a jPOS thread, so the decision about a purchase is made in the code that called the MUX.
basis: section:9.4 An Exception in a jPOS Callback Drops the Link and Reaches No Caller
aspects.reason: which threads Spring observes is not a behaviour an offline unit test can grade; the practices make the decision in the client, where it belongs

aspects.says: An answer with no field 39 or with a code not on the list decides nothing, and is treated like no answer and reversed.
basis: section:9.3 Field 39 Says Who Acts Next
section:9.8 Design Note: Why Reverse an Answer You Can't Read?
